title: A channel with backpressure
summary: Build a bounded async queue whose producers wait when it is full, the same contract that keeps streams from exhausting memory.
prompt:
Finish `Channel<T>(capacity)`:
- `send(value)` returns a promise. If fewer than `capacity` values are buffered (or a receiver is already waiting), it resolves at once. Otherwise it waits until a `receive` makes room: that is backpressure.
- `receive()` returns a promise of the oldest value. If the buffer is empty it waits for the next `send`.
- `size` is the number of buffered values.

Values must come out in the order they were sent, including values whose senders were waiting.
hints: Keep three FIFO arrays: buffered values, waiting receivers, and waiting senders as `{ value, resolve }`.
`send`: hand the value straight to a waiting receiver if there is one; else buffer it if there is room; else park the sender.
`receive`: take from the buffer and then move one parked sender's value into the buffer and resolve that sender.
